samuel2.15.p1.b1.text: Some time later, Absalom provided for himself a chariot with horses and fifty men to run ahead of him.

samuel2.15.p1.b3.text: “Look, your claims are good and right, but the king has no deputy to hear you.”

samuel2.15.p1.b4.text: “If only someone would appoint me judge in the land, then everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to me, and I would give him justice.”

samuel2.15.p2.b1.text: Also, when anyone approached to bow down to him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.

samuel2.15.p2.b2.text: Absalom did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for justice. In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

samuel2.15.p3.b1.text: “Please let me go to Hebron to fulfill a vow I have made to the LORD.”

samuel2.15.p3.b4.text: So the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept increasing.

samuel2.15.p4.b1.text: “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”

samuel2.15.p4.b2.text: “Arise and let us flee, or we will not escape from Absalom! We must leave quickly, or he will soon overtake us …”

samuel2.15.p4.b3.text: “Whatever our lord the king decides, we are your servants.”

samuel2.15.p4.b4.text: Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him. But he left behind ten concubines to take care of the palace.

samuel2.15.p5.b1.text: So the king set out with all the people following him. He stopped at the last house,

samuel2.15.p5.b2.text: All his servants marched past him … and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.

samuel2.15.p6.b1.text: “Why should you also go with us? Go back and stay with the new king, since you are both a foreigner and an exile from your homeland.”

samuel2.15.p6.b2.text: “… should I make you wander around with us today while I do not know where I am going? … May the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness.”

samuel2.15.p6.b3.text: “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!”

samuel2.15.p6.b4.text: So Ittai the Gittite marched past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.

samuel2.15.p7.b1.text: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly …

samuel2.15.p7.b2.text: … as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.

samuel2.15.p8.b1.text: Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God …

samuel2.15.p8.b2.text: “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.”

samuel2.15.p8.b3.text: But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”

samuel2.15.p9.b1.text: “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace—you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.”

samuel2.15.p9.b2.text: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”

samuel2.15.p9.b3.text: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there.

samuel2.15.p10.b1.text: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.

samuel2.15.p10.b2.text: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.”

samuel2.15.p10.b3.text: “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”

samuel2.15.p11.b1.text: When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.

samuel2.15.p11.b2.text: “But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; …’”

samuel2.15.p11.b3.text: “Send them to me with everything you hear.”

samuel2.15.p11.b4.text: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city.
